how: Les Francais Volants train at the Accor Arena rink (12e) with a hockey school open to all from age 3, and Patinoire Pailleron (19e) runs an ice school with adult groups.
Taekwondo Club Saint-Germain Paris (founded 1985) and several municipal-hall associations teach adult beginners, with trial classes offered.
Introductory dives (bapteme) run in the 20 m deep dive pit at Villeneuve-la-Garenne, about 10 km north of the centre, with instructor and gear supplied.
The City of Paris runs beginner adult ballet classes (Vaugirard-Littre gym on Sundays, Saturday beginner workshop) and associations such as MAKO Danse (19e) offer adult beginner classes.
Several studios in Paris (Atelier Setsuko, Studio Inoui, Atelier Arts Rose Selavy) teach wheel throwing, from single 2-3 hour introductions to multi-week courses.
4PADEL Paris 20 has three bookable pickleball courts and the Pickleball Paris club runs open-play lunchtime sessions in gyms; Issy-les-Moulineaux also has courts.
Schools such as DJ Network (3-hour weekend initiation), All Music Four School and Rythmik Academy teach DJing on turntables and CDJs, plus private tutors.
Pole Dance Paris runs small-group pole classes for all levels in three studios on rue d'Avron near Nation.
ANGA Capoeira Paris, Jogaki (free trial class) and Vida de Capoeira run adult capoeira classes in several districts.
Municipal Padel Ladoumegue (19e) plus private indoor clubs (Paris Padel, Les Padelistes, Forest Hill Aquaboulevard) rent courts and racquets.
Flamenco en France (11e) and Ida Flamenca (6e/7e) offer weekly adult flamenco dance classes at several levels, with trial classes.
Glassblowing introduction workshops (2-3 hours, make a piece to take home) are bookable through Wecandoo with artisans in Arcueil and Paris.
PUC Ultimate (Paris 13e), Lutece Ultimate and other clubs in Paris and Montrouge run recreational and competitive ultimate with beginner-friendly training.
Swing Cotton (Studio Breguet, 11e), Paris Anim' Bessie Smith and Brotherswing teach beginner Lindy Hop courses and discovery classes.
Paris Anim' centres (e.g. Wangari Maathai, 20e), the Village de cirque (12e) and Colectivo Newen run aerial fabric (tissu aerien) classes and workshops for adults.
The only curling club in Ile-de-France is in Viry-Chatillon (Essonne), with introductory sessions by arrangement rather than open walk-in play.
Breakin'13 (13e) runs weekly breakdance classes for children, teens and adults with a free trial class, and Paris Anim' centres offer beginner breaking courses.
Anusha Cherer teaches Bharatanatyam in Paris with beginner classes on Wednesday evenings in the 10e and intermediate classes on Saturdays in the 18e, via the Shantam association.
Triwat International teaches Kathak, Bollywood and Indian folk dance classes and workshops in Paris, and a Kathak teacher is listed at Espace Sylvia Monfort (15e).
Beginner silver jewellery workshops (rings, bracelets, hoops; 1.5-3 hours, work taken home) run in Paris 9e, 16e and 18e, plus a 70-hour professional jewellery course.
Tiffany copper-foil stained glass introductions (3-4 hours, make a panel to take home) are offered in Paris 17e, and A Fleur de Verre (3e) and Paris Ateliers teach the technique.
Meetup groups and bars such as Jovial (19e), Au Bonheur des Jeux de Societe and English-speaking Boardgamers of Paris host board game nights several times a week.
venue: Jovial Bar a Jeux de Societe

how: The Rencontres d'echecs Meetup group holds chess meetups in Paris cafes (Cafe Cayo, The Irishman) and in Montreuil and Asnieres-sur-Seine.
English-speaking Roleplayers of Paris and Tables ouvertes au De 12 host open tabletop RPG tables and campaigns in Paris.
Regular developer meetups run in Paris, such as Rust Paris and the C++ Francophone user group.
Paris Indie Games Developers (PIGD) meets at the Cite des Sciences et de l'Industrie; a game-development community exists though no jam event was seen.
Paris Cockerels (founded about 1998, oldest active French Australian football club) train and play at Stade du Polygone in Vincennes with a second team, the Cockatoos.
Perfume-making workshops (1-3 hours, leave with your own bottle) run at Molinard (1er), Galimard (9e), 5eme Sens (7e) and a parfumeur studio in the 4e.
Beginner-friendly amateur choirs include the Choeur de la Cite internationale (about 100 singers, all levels) and Le Sacre-Coeur choir (drop-in rehearsals on Tuesdays).
Angling is allowed on the Seine quays, Canal Saint-Martin, Canal de l'Ourcq and the Bois lakes with a day card (about 10 EUR); the federation runs Tuesday-evening street-fishing afterworks.

Freshwater coarse fishing is practised in the Seine, Marne, canals and lake ponds with a day or annual card; the FIAAPPMA 75-92-93-94 federation runs street-fishing afterworks (Tuesdays, May to November).
venue: Union des Pecheurs de Paris et de la Seine

how: Beginner tufting workshops (2-3 hours, use a tufting gun and take home a small rug) run at Tufting Studio and with independent studios in Paris 1er, 5e and 14e.
Une Maille a l'Endroit (shops in Paris and the inner suburbs) teaches 1.5-hour knitting and crochet classes for beginners, and the Brin de Cousette haberdashery runs classes.
Beginner hand-embroidery workshops (2.5-3 hours, materials provided) run in Paris 8e and 11e (Boutique Flanelle), with longer gold-embroidery courses at GRETA (10e).
Scented-candle workshops (1.5-3 hours, take home your candles) are bookable across Paris in the 2e, 5e, 11e, 13e, 15e and 20e arrondissements.
Chocolate workshops (tablets and truffles, 1-2 hours, from prepared couverture; also at the Musee du Chocolat) run in central Paris; no bean-to-bar roasting course was seen.
Two-hour cocktail workshops with a bartender (Parisian Cocktail Club, Colada, Les Raffineurs, La compagnie du mieux boire) run across the 2e, 8e, 11e, 15e and 18e.

activity: Hands-on cooking classes (pasta and other cuisines)
how: Hands-on cooking classes cover pasta and ravioli (2e, 4e), Japanese, Vietnamese and Thai cuisine in many arrondissements.
Sushi workshops with tasting are held in Paris 6e (traditional sushi) and at Le Labo Culinaire (17e).
The Societe astronomique de France, headquartered in Paris, runs observation sessions, courses and monthly lectures for amateurs.
